hero.title: AI Use Policy for General-Purpose AI
hero.tagline: From regulatory risk to enterprise asset
hero.body: In Europe, expectations for general-purpose AI are clear. The EU AI Act and the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice require companies to govern how AI is used. An AI Use Policy is the foundation: a legally aligned, technically informed document that sets boundaries, roles, and controls for AI in your company.

facts.title: Mandatory by implication
facts.value: Internal governance expected by the AI Act
facts.description: The AI Act expects oversight, transparency, risk mitigation, and clear roles. A documented policy is how you meet and prove these expectations.

facts.title: Enterprise deal enabler
facts.description: Buyers ask for evidence of responsible AI. A signed policy shows your controls are clear and enforceable.

facts.title: Risk containment
facts.value: Protect data, IP, and compliance posture
facts.description: Prevent misuse of confidential data, biased outputs, sector rule breaches, and enforcement risk under the AI Act and GDPR.

deliverables.title: A policy that enables compliant innovation
deliverables.body: Clarity for teams, assurance for customers, and a defensible position for auditors and regulators. A minimum investment that returns in faster sales cycles, fewer escalations, and safer AI use.

sections.title: 1. Scope and objectives
sections.desc: Applies to employees, contractors, and vendors. Defines GPAI and the systems in scope across products and internal use.

sections.title: 2. Roles and responsibilities
sections.desc: Accountability for providers, deployers, and users; RACI for approvals, monitoring, and incident handling.
bullets: Model owner, product owner, compliance owner

sections.title: 3. Permitted use and controls
sections.desc: Allowed tools, datasets, and tasks by team; prohibited uses; data handling rules for prompts and outputs.

sections.title: 4. Transparency and human oversight
sections.desc: User-facing disclosures, content attribution rules, and review steps before high-impact use.

sections.title: 5. Monitoring, training, and updates
sections.desc: Review cadence, policy change control, and links to training logs and risk registers.

cta.title: A minimum investment, a high-return asset
cta.body: The cost of not having an AI Use Policy is measured in delays, fines, and lost opportunities. The cost of having one is modest, especially when it enables faster sales cycles, reduced exposure, smoother adoption, and a trustworthy AI-enabled brand.
